key_insight: X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism (XDP) shows a clear tau pathology signature, with imbalanced tau isoforms and accumulation of hyperphosphorylated 4-repeat tau, especially in astrocytes.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest tau dysregulation may be a core disease mechanism in XDP and could help identify biomarkers or pathways relevant to related neurodegenerative disorders.
method: Analyzed striatal brain tissue for tau misfolding, phosphorylation, and MAPT exon 10 inclusion.
Profiled transcriptomic changes across brain regions to map tau-related pathway dysregulation.
Measured plasma pTau181, GFAP, and neurofilament light chain in patients and controls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports correlations with repeat length in the causal insertion, cross-brain transcriptomic dysregulation, and plasma biomarkers that discriminated XDP from controls.
watch_item: The findings are based on a specific rare genetic disease cohort, so broader generalization and biomarker performance will need validation in independent and larger populations.
paper_title: Tau isoform imbalance and aggregation are pathological hallmarks of X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism
